answer: Each agent is a vessel that must dock at a public jetty once per epoch and show a chain of raven receipts: signed delivery confirmations from distinct counterparties reached across a bridge to a second network. Every receipt costs its sender a small fee and binds one identity key, one counterparty and one epoch, so it cannot be copied to a clone. A fake identity needs its own fresh chain each epoch, paying real counterparties each time; cost scales per clone, and pooling collapses because one receipt never attests two vessels.
